input.quote: Following the expiration of the Term pursuant to clause (a) (but not clause (b)) of Section 12.1.1, the grants in Section 5.1.3 shall become non-exclusive, fully-paid, royalty-free and irrevocable.
input.rationale: The IP package sits at (and in parts above) our fallback, so we are not redlining it. (1) Harpoon retains ownership of its own platform know-how and inventions (7.1.1, p0427–p0428; 5.6.1 retention of rights), which is the permitted "vendor keeps generic tools and know-how" outcome. (2) AbbVie's licence to the licensed subject matter is exclusive, worldwide (Territory = "the entire world"), covers full Exploitation of Licensed Compounds and Licensed Products (5.1.3(a), p0355) including Development and Manufacture, and is sublicensable through multiple tiers to Affiliates and other Persons (5.3, p0359); on expiry of the Term it becomes "non-exclusive, fully-paid, royalty-free and irrevocable" (12.1.2, p0583), i.e. perpetual, irrevocable and royalty-free. Royalties during the Royalty Term are the negotiated price of the licence, not an IP-direction defect, so we note but do not flag the gap against the fallback's "royalty-free" wording. (3) Nothing assigns AbbVie IP or data to Harpoon; conversely AbbVie owns all Regulatory Documentation in the Territory (3.8.2(c), p0327) and the Product Trademarks (7.6, p0485). (4) Harpoon's only licence in AbbVie material is the narrow 5.2 grant (p0358) — non-exclusive, royalty-free, no sublicensing, to Develop and Manufacture "solely to the extent necessary for Harpoon to perform its obligations as set forth in, and subject to, the Initial Development Plan" — plus the mutual confidentiality use limit in 9.2; that is service delivery, not independent exploitation, so the Customer-data element is met. (5) Joint IP is created under 7.1.2 (p0429), which falls short of the preferred "no joint ownership", but each Party "shall have the right to Exploit the Joint Intellectual Property Rights without a duty of seeking consent from or accounting to the other Party", so this is not the walk-away (joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit) and the fallback contains no no-joint-ownership element. The redacted carve-outs at the end of 7.1.2 and in 12.7.1 (reversion licence) cannot be assessed from the text and should be confirmed commercially, but nothing visible breaches the fallback.
